domain: Legal Anthropology / Indigenous Law / Comparative Constitutional Theory
topic_summary: Analysis of contested readings of historical treaties between settler states and Indigenous nations. Settler-state legal regimes read treaties as finalized property transactions extinguishing Indigenous sovereign rights. Indigenous nations read the same treaties as living relational pacts for shared territorial stewardship. The competing readings instantiate structurally different constraints with different beneficiary/victim structures.

key_entities: Settler-state legal regimes (interpretive authority claiming Crown sovereignty)
Indigenous nations (interpretive authority claiming continuing sovereignty)
key_tensions: Finalized transaction vs living relationship (ontological difference in what treaties ARE)
key_mechanisms: Settler-state judicial interpretation (courts applying extinguishment doctrine)
Indigenous treaty practice (ceremonial renewal, relational obligations)
key_absences: Treaty negotiation context (power asymmetries, translation failures, oral vs written)
Contemporary resource extraction regimes built on extinguishment reading
Indigenous legal orders as parallel rather than subordinate systems

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Historical treaties as shared commitment substrate—the same documents held by both parties as authoritative but read to generate opposing constraints
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Dual authority structure: settler courts claim interpretive monopoly via Crown sovereignty; Indigenous nations claim interpretive authority via continuing sovereignty and treaty partner status
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Interpretive Capture — settler legal system denies revision while absorbing drift through judicial 'interpretation' that functionally rewrites without surfacing as revision

readings.commitment: Treaties as completed property transactions—Indigenous parties ceded territorial sovereignty in exchange for defined reserves and payments
readings.authority_grounding: Settler-state courts claiming Crown sovereignty and juridical finality
readings.expected_structural_delta: Indigenous nations exit victim set for territorial jurisdiction; enter beneficiary set for narrow treaty rights (reserves, annuities); settler state becomes sole legitimate authority over ceded territory

readings.commitment: Treaties as relational pacts for shared territorial stewardship—no cession of sovereignty, mutual obligations for coexistence
readings.authority_grounding: Indigenous legal orders and treaty oral traditions claiming continuing sovereignty
readings.expected_structural_delta: Indigenous nations remain in beneficiary set for territorial jurisdiction; settler state enters obligation set for consent and shared governance; territorial resources become jointly managed rather than unilaterally extracted

readings.commitment: Treaties as international agreements between sovereign equals—requiring ongoing consent and subject to modern treaty law principles
readings.authority_grounding: International law frameworks (UNDRIP, treaty law principles) and Indigenous constitutional traditions
readings.expected_structural_delta: Indigenous nations enter beneficiary set as co-equal sovereigns with consent rights over territorial changes; settler state constrained by international treaty obligations; unilateral resource extraction becomes treaty violation

axiom_contradictions.basis: Extinguishment axiom (territorial sovereignty can be permanently transferred via treaty) cannot coexist with stewardship axiom (sovereignty is inalienable and treaties create shared obligations not transfers) in any single coherent framework—accepting one requires rejecting the other

Extinguishment axiom (treaties finalize status and are not revisable except by settler state) contradicts nation-to-nation axiom (treaties between sovereigns require ongoing consent and remain subject to treaty law)—no framework can hold both as simultaneously true

axes.human_readable: Extinguishment Reading (Treaties as Completed Property Transactions)
axes.structural_delta: Treaties interpreted as finalized cessions of territorial sovereignty in exchange for defined reserves and payments
axes.primary_observable: Judicial doctrine prevalence; resource extraction permits issued without Indigenous consent; territorial jurisdiction exercised unilaterally
axes.selection_reason: Dominant institutional reading; high extractiveness; benefits settler resource economy at cost of Indigenous jurisdiction

axes.human_readable: Stewardship Reading (Treaties as Living Relational Pacts)
axes.structural_delta: Treaties interpreted as ongoing mutual obligations for shared territorial stewardship without sovereignty cession
axes.primary_observable: Indigenous legal practices (ceremonial renewal, consent protocols); community resistance to extraction; alternative governance proposals
axes.selection_reason: Structurally distinct observable (relational practice vs juridical doctrine); coordination rather than extraction logic; sibling reading to extinguishment

axes.human_readable: Nation-to-Nation Reading (Treaties as International Agreements Between Sovereigns)
axes.structural_delta: Treaties interpreted through international law frameworks requiring ongoing consent and sovereign equality
axes.primary_observable: UNDRIP implementation; consent-based resource agreements; international legal advocacy; parallel governance structures
axes.selection_reason: Introduces international law dimension; structurally distinct authority grounding; provides third vertex for constraint topology

axes.human_readable: Translation Substrate Erosion (Oral vs Written Treaty Divergence)
axes.structural_delta: Systematic divergence between oral Indigenous understandings and written English/French texts treated as authoritative
axes.primary_observable: Linguistic analysis of treaty texts; oral history records; documented translation failures during negotiations
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: upstream substrate that feeds all readings but contributes limited independent analytical yield beyond kernel recognition itself

axes.human_readable: Resource Extraction Lock-In (Economic Dependence on Extinguishment Regime)
axes.structural_delta: Settler-state economy structurally dependent on resource extraction premised on extinguishment reading
axes.primary_observable: GDP composition from extractive industries on treaty territory; infrastructure investments assuming unilateral jurisdiction
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: downstream consequence rather than independent reading; captured via extinguishment_reading's beneficiary structure

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Systematic oral vs written treaty text divergence
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Upstream substrate feeding all readings but limited independent yield beyond kernel recognition

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Economic dependence on extraction premised on extinguishment
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Downstream consequence captured via extinguishment_reading's beneficiary/victim structure

omegas.description: Does settler judicial 'reconciliation' doctrine constitute covert revision of extinguishment reading, or reinforcement through partial accommodation? If revision, drift_status should be 'partial' not 'absent'.
omegas.source: Commitment system drift assessment; judicial cases like Haida Nation, Tsilhqot'in

omegas.description: Is stewardship_reading truly a Rope (coordination without extraction) or does it become a Tangled_Rope when institutionalized through co-management regimes that preserve settler veto power?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) applied to institutionalized stewardship

omegas.description: Is nation_to_nation_reading a true Scaffold (building toward alternative structure) or merely aspirational if international law lacks enforcement mechanism against settler states?
omegas.source: Hypothesis classification uncertainty; UNDRIP non-binding status

omegas.description: Considered 'pragmatic accommodation reading' (treaties as flexible instruments adjusted through negotiation) but collapsed into stewardship_reading—pragmatism without sovereignty recognition still instantiates stewardship constraint, just with weaker enforcement.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition confirmed genuine: extinguishment and stewardship readings instantiate structurally different constraints (different victim/beneficiary sets, different epsilon structures). Nation-to-nation reading introduces third vertex via international law authority structure. All three readings proceed to generation as specified in §1.3-K.
